turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come, sit. What is the problem today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Sorry doctor, the auto got stuck at the signal and we are late. Umm, there is a lump on my neck.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Since when?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Three weeks. I saw it in the mirror while getting ready for office and I thought, mosquito bite only, but it did not go.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I saw it also, doctor. Three weeks, around that only.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is it painful?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Our neighbour's cat, the ginger one, she scratched me. I was just giving milk and she turned nasty, what to say.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): I asked about the lump. Pain, yes or no?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, sorry. No, no pain. It is just there, not paining.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fever now?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever now. I checked at home, thermometer was normal only.
[SEG0012] person_3 (CAREGIVER): One night the pillow was wet, doctor. He was sweating. Only that one night.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Night sweats just once?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm. Once only. After that sleep was fine, I even saw the cricket and dozed off.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Cough?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any weight loss?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Err, I ate too many laddoos if anything. The tiredness is there though.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tired since when?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Since Diwali or after, I cannot say. I don't keep dates.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Trouble swallowing?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Of. No. Swallowing is normal. I had chai and a samosa on the way, no issue.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): The scratch is still there?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Left forearm, a small line is still there. Umm, ten days back, or the Sunday before, I mix it up.
[SEG0025] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Sunday before last. I put turmeric, it is drying only.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any lump in the armpit or groin?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Only this one on the neck.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Which tablets are you taking?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Metformine 500 mg morning and night, for the sugar. And Omprazole 20 mg on empty stomach, for the burning.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): That acidity is old, last winter, or the one before. I really cannot place it.
[SEG0031] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Mizartan also, for the pressure, 40 mg after dinner. I keep the strip.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Diabetes and blood pressure, both ongoing. Any reaction to a drug, ever?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): No, never. I have taken penicillin, amoxicillin for the tooth, and everything was fine. No rash, nothing.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. I will examine the neck now.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Two centimetre node, right side of the neck, mobile, not tender. Skin over it looks normal. No other nodes in the neck.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Temperature 36.8, pulse 84, blood pressure 128 over 78. Left forearm scratch is a faint healing line, not infected.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Is it cancer? My uncle had TB and coughed for months, so my mother sent Lakshmi with me. Traffic was mad today also, I am telling you.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am not saying cancer. Most likely a reactive node, possibly from the cat scratch, but that one night sweat means I cannot rule out tuberculosis.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok. So sonography or what? Should I stop the laddoos?
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blood tests, full count and ESR, and an ultrasound of the neck. I am booking both.
[SEG0041] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Today itself?
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): Bloods today, downstairs. Ultrasound tomorrow morning.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do not keep pressing the lump. If you get high fever or the lump grows quickly, come sooner. Otherwise I will see you in one week with the reports.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, office I can go? And the cat, I should avoid her?
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Office is fine. Do not let the cat scratch you again. Continue Metformine, Omprazole and the pressure tablet. No new medicine today.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Mizartan I sometimes forget on Sundays, when I go to my cousin. Is that bad?
[SEG0047] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Most Sundays he misses it. I keep telling him.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Then I cannot be sure it is taken as prescribed. Take it every night, Sundays included.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Achha, every night. Sonography, I come fasting?
[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): No fasting for the neck ultrasound. The blood count also does not need fasting.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok doctor. Lakshmi, we will take the bus, auto will charge extra now.
[SEG0052] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Next time I will bring the Mizartan box, so the name on it is clear.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, bring the box. We are done.

spec.situation: Young adult with a painless neck lump for three weeks, night sweats once, no fever now; recent cat scratch mentioned; doctor examines and orders blood tests and ultrasound.

traps.happens: The transcript looks like speech-to-text: drug names are sometimes spelled wrongly ('Omprazole', 'Mizartan' for telmisartan, 'Metformine'), fragments and fillers appear ('Err', 'Of.', 'Mm.', 'Umm'), numbers are sometimes digits and sometimes words.
traps.label_rule: Medicine names are recorded as written in the transcript (name) with a normalized/generic name ONLY when the true drug is certain from context (a drug 'for the pressure' written 'Mizartan' is NOT certain enough: leave generic_name empty). Fragments and fillers are never facts.

traps.happens: The doctor asks about drug reactions. Variants (use ONE per encounter): (a) the patient says 'No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything' (no allergy); (b) the patient is unsure ('maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which'); (c) a real allergy with the reaction described; (d) allergies are never asked.
traps.label_rule: (a) NO allergy entry: negative_findings 'Allergies' absent. (b) allergy with status uncertain, the substance as described, the reaction if said, plus an allergy_uncertain uncertainty. (c) allergy with the reaction. (d) nothing at all. NEVER list a medicine the patient has taken without a reaction as an allergy, and the plan must not prescribe a drug of a recorded allergy's family.

features: patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.

omissions.text: Omeprazole 20 mg is taken on an empty stomach.
No new medicine was prescribed today.
The patient sometimes, and per caregiver most Sundays, misses the Mizartan dose on Sundays.
The neck lump is specifically not painful ('no pain').
The patient reported normal temperature checked at home with a thermometer.
The patient denied any lump in the armpit or groin, saying only the neck lump is present.
Drug allergy history included tolerance of penicillin and amoxicillin without rash or other reaction.
On examination, the right neck node was described as a node/lymph node and measured 2 cm, mobile and not tender; this supports that it is a cervical lymph node rather than just a generic lump.
The left forearm scratch was described by the doctor as a faint healing line, not infected.
The doctor advised to come sooner specifically for high fever or if the lump grows quickly.
Follow-up was to be in one week with the reports.
